## Harsha Lake emission driver maps  

Spatially explicit maps of several drivers of the CH~4~ total emission rate random forest model were constructed for William H Harsha lake in southwest Ohio (lake_id == 1031 in dataset). Bathymetry was retrieved from the Ohio Department of Natural Resources Geospatial Data Portal and point measurements of chlorophyll-*a*, turbidity, and surface water temperature in June 2014  were retrieved from Beck et al [-@beck_2016]. Point measurements of dissolved oxygen and water temperature between June and August of 2015 were retrieved from Beaulieu et al [-@beaulieu_etal_2018]. Heat map were constructed by 1) fitting a spatial linear model (splm) to each data set using site depth as the predictor, 2) using the model to predict the value of each variable across spatial grid bounded by the lake perimeter. These spatially explicit datasets were subsequently used to inform predictions of the total CH~4~ emission rate at the lake. The splm and spatial predictions were executed using the spmodel [@dumelle_et_al_2023] package in R [@r_core_team_2025].
